root_cause: ACL 101 applied inbound on Gi0/1 is blocking traffic from 192.168.30.0/24 subnet.
evidence: show access-lists: 'deny ip 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 any' present in ACL 101 applied inbound on Gi0/1
fix_steps: Modify ACL 101 to permit traffic from 192.168.30.0/24 to the server subnet.
Re-apply the updated access-list on interface Gi0/1 inbound.
Verify connectivity from VLAN 30 PC to the server using ping.

root_cause: SW1-SW2 trunk link does not allow VLAN 20 in its allowed VLAN list.
evidence: show interfaces trunk: SW1-SW2 trunk allowed vlans 1,10 (VLAN 20 missing from allowed list)
fix_steps: Access the trunk interfaces on SW1 and SW2.
Execute 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20' on both sides.
Verify with 'show interfaces trunk' that VLAN 20 is allowed and forwarding.

root_cause: Incorrect default gateway configured on PC3 (set to 192.168.10.254 instead of 192.168.10.1).
evidence: show ip interface brief on PC3: IP 192.168.10.5, Gateway configured as 192.168.10.254 (does not match R1's actual interface IP 192.168.10.1)
fix_steps: Open IP configuration settings on PC3.
Update default gateway address to 192.168.10.1.
Test gateway ping from PC3.

root_cause: Parent physical interface GigabitEthernet0/0 on R1 is administratively down.
evidence: show ip interface brief on R1: GigabitEthernet0/0 status administratively down, protocol down
fix_steps: Enter interface configuration mode for GigabitEthernet0/0 on R1.
Run the 'no shutdown' command.
Confirm interface and subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 state changes to up/up.

root_cause: The DHCP pool for VLAN30 has exhausted all available IP addresses.
evidence: show ip dhcp pool VLAN30: Total addresses 10, Leased addresses 10, Available 0
fix_steps: Expand the subnet scope for dhcp pool VLAN30 on R1.
Clear inactive DHCP leases using 'clear ip dhcp binding *' if applicable.
Verify pool availability with 'show ip dhcp pool VLAN30'.

root_cause: Physical cable disconnection between the VLAN40 PCs and the access switch is preventing DHCP discovery packets from reaching R1.
evidence: ipconfig on PC: APIPA address 169.254.x.x assigned
fix_steps: Re-seat or replace the Ethernet cable between the PC and the access switch.
Verify link light status on the switch port.
Retry DHCP renewal on the PC.

root_cause: PC is configured with an incorrect/unreachable DNS server IP (8.8.4.8 instead of 8.8.8.8).
evidence: show ip interface brief on PC: DNS server configured as 8.8.4.8 (unreachable, typo); ping 8.8.4.8 request timed out
fix_steps: Open network adapter DNS settings on PC.
Change primary DNS server IP to 8.8.8.8.
Test domain name resolution using ping or nslookup.

root_cause: R1 lacks a routing table entry to reach the HQ DNS server network (10.0.0.53/32).
evidence: show ip route on R1: no route to 10.0.0.53/32 (DNS server subnet); ping 10.0.0.53 from R1 fails
fix_steps: Configure a static route or enable dynamic routing protocol propagation to 10.0.0.0/24 on R1.
Verify reachability with 'ping 10.0.0.53' from R1.
Test DNS resolution from Branch PCs.

root_cause: Appears to be a generic Layer 3 connectivity issue, possibly related to ACL filtering between the branch and HQ.
evidence: show ip route on R1: no entry for 172.16.0.0/24 (HQ subnet)
fix_steps: Review ACLs applied on R1 and R2 for statements blocking the HQ subnet.
Check inbound and outbound ACL direction on relevant interfaces.
Retest connectivity after any ACL changes.

root_cause: Routing loop caused by misconfigured next-hop on R2 pointing back to R1 for subnet 172.16.0.0/24.
evidence: show ip route on R2: static route 172.16.0.0/24 via R1 (should be via R3); show ip route on R1: static route back via R2 for same network
fix_steps: Remove incorrect static route on R2: 'no ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.255.0 <R1-IP>'.
Add correct static route on R2 pointing to R3.
Run traceroute to verify loop resolution.

root_cause: Guest SSID is assigned to default VLAN 1 and lacks access restrictions to internal subnets.
evidence: show access-lists GUEST_ISOLATION: ACL has no deny entry for internal server subnet; show vlan brief: guest SSID mapped to VLAN 1 instead of dedicated guest VLAN
fix_steps: Re-map guest SSID to dedicated Guest VLAN.
Update GUEST_ISOLATION ACL to deny traffic to internal server subnets.
Apply updated ACL to guest interface/VLAN.

root_cause: Access list 105 is not applied to vty lines using 'access-class' command.
evidence: show access-lists 105: 'deny tcp any any eq 23' present but show run | section line vty shows 'access-class' not applied to vty 0 4
fix_steps: Enter line configuration mode: 'line vty 0 4'.
Apply access list using 'access-class 105 in'.
Test Telnet connection to verify access restriction.

root_cause: Wildcard mask 0.0.0.15 in ACL 110 restricts permitted range to 192.168.1.0-192.168.1.15 instead of /24.
evidence: show access-lists 110: 'permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.15 any' (wildcard mask too restrictive, only covers .0-.15)
fix_steps: Remove incorrect permit rule from ACL 110.
Add rule 'permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any' with correct wildcard mask.
Verify traffic from hosts in range .16-.254.

root_cause: NAT inside/outside commands are not applied to R1 interfaces.
evidence: show ip nat translations: empty; show run | section nat: 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside' not applied to any interface
fix_steps: Apply 'ip nat inside' on the LAN interface of R1.
Apply 'ip nat outside' on the WAN/ISP interface of R1.
Verify translation generation using 'show ip nat translations'.

root_cause: NAT translation table timeout or a general ACL match issue is preventing new translations from being created.
evidence: show ip nat statistics: pool addresses exhausted
fix_steps: Review the NAT ACL for incorrect permit/deny statements.
Clear existing NAT translations with 'clear ip nat translation *'.
Retest and monitor 'show ip nat statistics' for translation failures.

root_cause: Switch port FastEthernet0/5 is administratively shut down.
evidence: show interfaces Fa0/5: Fa0/5 is administratively down, line protocol is down
fix_steps: Enter configuration mode for interface FastEthernet0/5 on SW1.
Execute 'no shutdown'.
Confirm physical link status changes to up/up.

root_cause: Duplex mismatch between SW1 Fa0/6 (half-duplex) and SW2 Fa0/1 (full-duplex).
evidence: show interfaces Fa0/6: 100Mb/s, half-duplex; show interfaces Fa0/1 on SW2: 100Mb/s, full-duplex
fix_steps: Access interface Fa0/6 on SW1.
Set duplex mode to full: 'duplex full' (or set auto-negotiation on both ends).
Verify duplex alignment and confirm absence of interface collision errors.

root_cause: Subnet mask configured on PC is /30 (255.255.255.252) instead of /24 (255.255.255.0).
evidence: show ip interface brief on PC: subnet mask 255.255.255.252 (/30) instead of 255.255.255.0 (/24), splitting the subnet incorrectly
fix_steps: Open IP configuration settings on PC.
Update subnet mask to 255.255.255.0.
Test ping connectivity to other PCs in 192.168.5.0/24.

root_cause: Switch port physical cable is intermittently disconnected or the interface is experiencing hardware failure.
evidence: show arp on SW1: 192.168.1.50 mapped to two different MAC addresses at different times
fix_steps: Re-seat cabling on the affected switch ports.
Swap the suspect cable with a known-good one.
Monitor 'show interfaces' for CRC/input errors.

root_cause: Spanning Tree port costs are unadjusted, causing STP to block the 1Gb link instead of the 100Mb link.
evidence: show spanning-tree vlan 10: one trunk port role is 'Blocking' as expected by STP, but the active link is the lower-bandwidth 100Mb link instead of the 1Gb link (port cost not tuned)
fix_steps: Adjust STP port cost on 100Mb interface or lower port cost on 1Gb interface.
Verify STP topology state with 'show spanning-tree vlan 10'.
Confirm 1Gb interface is in Forwarding state.

root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch across trunk link (SW1 native VLAN 1 vs SW2 native VLAN 99).
evidence: show interfaces trunk: SW1 native VLAN 1, SW2 native VLAN 99 on the same trunk link; %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH logged
fix_steps: Access switchport configuration on SW1 and SW2 trunk ports.
Set matching native VLAN on both sides (e.g., 'switchport trunk native vlan 99').
Verify CDP native VLAN mismatch errors cease.

root_cause: SSID broadcast is disabled ('no broadcast-ssid') on Access Point AP1.
evidence: show run | section wlan: SSID 'Corp-WiFi' configured with 'no broadcast-ssid' (hidden network) though users expect it to be visible
fix_steps: Enter WLAN configuration mode for 'Corp-WiFi' on AP1.
Enable SSID broadcasting.
Verify SSID visibility on wireless client devices.

root_cause: WPA2 Pre-Shared Key mismatch between AP configuration ('Cisco123') and distributed client password ('Cisco1234').
evidence: show run | section wlan: pre-shared key configured as 'Cisco123' but the documented/distributed password is 'Cisco1234' (mismatch)
fix_steps: Update pre-shared key on AP1 to match intended password ('Cisco1234').
Save WLAN configuration.
Reconnect client devices using distributed password.

root_cause: Co-channel interference caused by neighboring APs (AP1 and AP2) both operating on channel 6.
evidence: show wlan statistics: AP1 and AP2 both configured on channel 6 (overlapping), high co-channel interference reported
fix_steps: Change radio channel of AP2 to a non-overlapping channel (e.g., channel 1 or 11).
Verify interference levels drop in 'show wlan statistics'.
Test client stability on both APs.

root_cause: Switch port Fa0/4 was not assigned to VLAN 60 and remains in default VLAN 1.
evidence: show run | section Gi0/0: Gi0/0.60 encapsulation dot1Q 60, ip address 192.168.60.254/24 -- but 'show vlan brief' shows Fa0/4 (VLAN60 host port) missing from VLAN60, still in default VLAN 1
fix_steps: Access interface Fa0/4 configuration on SW1.
Run 'switchport access vlan 60'.
Confirm Fa0/4 assignment under 'show vlan brief' and test ping to subinterface.

root_cause: HSRP preempt is disabled and priorities are set to default (100) on both R1 and R2.
evidence: show standby brief: R1 priority 100 (default), R2 priority 100 (default), preempt disabled on both -- failover relies on hello/hold timers only
fix_steps: Increase primary router priority on R1: 'standby 1 priority 110'.
Enable preempt on primary and standby routers: 'standby 1 preempt'.
Test failover delay using interface shutdown.

root_cause: Trunk encapsulation dot1Q negotiation failure between the switches is causing the port to go down.
evidence: show interfaces Fa0/8 status: err-disabled
fix_steps: Verify trunk encapsulation settings match on both switches.
Hard-code encapsulation dot1q on the trunk ports.
Re-enable the port and monitor for further errors.

root_cause: ACL 120 is applied inbound on WAN interface Gi0/1 instead of outbound on LAN or outbound on WAN.
evidence: show run | interface Gi0/1: 'ip access-group 120 in' (ACL 120 was written to filter outbound LAN traffic but applied inbound on the WAN interface)
fix_steps: Remove ACL 120 from Gi0/1 inbound using 'no ip access-group 120 in'.
Apply ACL 120 on LAN interface Gi0/0 inbound or WAN Gi0/1 outbound as intended.
Verify external inbound traffic to LAN operates normally.

root_cause: SW1 management interface (Vlan1 SVI) is missing a default gateway configuration.
evidence: show ip interface brief on SW1: Vlan1 up/up, IP address 192.168.1.2, but no default gateway configured ('show ip default-gateway' returns none)
fix_steps: Configure default gateway on SW1: 'ip default-gateway 192.168.1.1'.
Verify configuration using 'show ip default-gateway'.
Test remote management access across subnets.

root_cause: NAT access-list only permits UDP traffic, preventing HTTP (TCP 80) and HTTPS (TCP 443) traffic from being translated.
evidence: ping dns_server_ip: successful; show ip nat translations: DNS traffic (UDP 53) is translated, but HTTP (TCP 80) and HTTPS (TCP 443) sessions show no translation entries; NAT ACL only permits UDP traffic
fix_steps: Update NAT ACL to permit all IP traffic (or include TCP ports 80/443).
Clear active NAT translations with 'clear ip nat translation *'.
Verify web browsing functionality and check 'show ip nat translations'.
